summary: Checked all ~48 doc groups added in this diff (class-level summaries, apply/accept/test/applyAsX method docs, @tparam/@param/@return tags) against the actual case-class and value-class bodies read directly from library/src/scala/jdk/FunctionWrappers.scala. Verified: (1) every FromJavaXxx case class's 'delegates to a Java Xxx' claim matches its extends clause and method body; (2) every AsJavaXxx case class's 'delegates to a Scala FunctionN' claim matches its body; (3) every RichXxxAsFunctionN / RichFunctionNAsXxx class doc correctly lists exactly the methods present (single asScala/asJava for primitive-only wrapper types with no generic type params, vs. asJava+asJavaXxx pairs for generic wrapper types) - confirmed via grep across all ~40 Rich* classes; (4) all 21 'explicitly named alias' asJavaXxx methods were individually diffed against their corresponding asJava method bodies and are structurally identical (same FromJavaXxx pattern match, same fallback), so the 'identical behavior' claim holds for every one, not just the first; (5) @return `()`, since the delegate is called only for its side effect' is correctly present only on Unit-returning accept/apply methods of Consumer-family types (16 occurrences), and correctly absent on non-Unit apply methods whose description already begins with 'Returns' and states the full return value, matching the project's @return-drop rule; (6) all repeated tparam/param tag groups (x1/x2 argument descriptions, underlying descriptions, T/U/R type-parameter descriptions) were checked against every listed occurrence's actual signature and fit in all cases, including the trickier ObjDoubleConsumer/ObjIntConsumer/ObjLongConsumer 'first (object) argument... second argument is a primitive' tparam text and the Function[T,R]-only tparam-T-and-R co-occurrence. No blockers or nits found; no pre-existing doc issues noticed outside the diff.
